response: Yes, even impaired fasting blood glucose levels preoperatively are associated with increased mortality after Coronary Artery Bypass Graft (CABG) surgery. The elevated risk of death after CABG surgery, previously known to be associated with confirmed diabetes mellitus, also appears to be shared by a group of similar size that includes patients with impaired fasting glucose (IFG) and undiagnosed diabetes mellitus. This suggests that preoperative impaired fasting blood glucose levels, even if not meeting the full criteria for diabetes, can be a significant risk factor for increased mortality after CABG surgery.
